newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power firm amid high fuel cost.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power firm amid high fuel cost.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. remained firm Thursday against Wednesday's levels amid high cost of fuels linked to strong natural gas and fuel oil prices, market sources said.
The domestic natgas market was supported by forecast of cold weather in the Midwest and lower-than-expected amount of gas injected into underground storage last week.
Swing natgas delivered to the New York City gate was quoted today at $2.75-$2.80 per million British thermal units.
Spot resid values stayed buoyant on unseasonal strength in crude prices driven by concerns over low heating oil stocks.
In the key New York harbor market, one percent sulphur resid grade, most used by electric utilities and industrial users, was assessed at $21.00-$21.50 a barrel.
But some participants emphasized tight generation capacity and ongoing contraints in transmission as the primary reasons for firm spot power values in the Northeast.
"The main factors are limited supply and transmission," said one Northeast trader.
The region's generation picture may ease with Friday's scheduled startup of the 510 megawatt (MW) Vermont Yankee nuclear power plant in Vernon, Vt., from refueling, market sources said.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Friday was assessed at $34.00-$35.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), a tighter range than Wednesday's $33.00-$35.00.
Non-firm, next-day NEPOOL power during off-peak hours was still valued at $21.00-$22.00.
In the New York Power Pool (NYPP), peak, non-firm electricity in the eastern part of the grid for Friday was pegged at $29.00-$30.00 a MWh, compared with a quoted of $29.50-$30.00 on Wednesday.
Off-peak, non-firm NYPP power into eastern NYPP for next-day delivery was flat from Wednesday at $17.00.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity prices were discussed at $19.00-$22.00 for Friday delivery, compared with a quote near $19.50 on Wednesday for Thursday.
Off-peak, non-firm power for delivery into western for Friday was assessed at $14.00-$15.00, wider than Wednesday's quote near $14.00.
Western NYPP electricity for the weekend was valued at $15.00-$18.00 a MWh.
